issues.title: Timestamp ties skip rows across pull pages
evidence: backend/database/change_feed.py:18 installs transaction-bound source triggers; backend/database/change_feed.py:138 pages by per-business revision rather than timestamp.
backend/routes/sync.py:886 selects protocol 2 and explicitly rejects legacy incremental/paginated peers with HTTP 426; backend/services/sync_worker.py:3289 retains its cursor on an incompatible peer.

backend/tests/test_sync_protocol_v2.py:57 verifies same-time ties and raw-SQL/backdated changes; :78 verifies the legacy upgrade hold. Included in the independently executed disposable PostgreSQL 11-pass run on 2026-10-31.
remaining: Deploy migrations and protocol-compatible server/device builds together. Legacy incremental clients deliberately pause until upgraded; production deployment was not performed.

issues.title: Response-end watermark misses writes during table reads
evidence: backend/database/change_feed.py:18 captures insert/update/delete in the source transaction. PostgreSQL increments a per-business clock while holding its row lock through commit; SQLite serializes writers.
backend/database/change_feed.py:138 acknowledges only visible committed event revisions, independent of source timestamps and client clock skew.

backend/tests/test_sync_protocol_v2.py:57 verifies a raw-SQL write with a backdated timestamp after an acknowledged page; :175 uses real concurrent PostgreSQL transactions and verifies that the second writer cannot publish a later revision before its predecessor commits. Both passed in the 11-test constrained-role run.
remaining: No production contention/throughput measurement or long-running operational soak was performed. Database deadlock/transaction retry handling remains the normal writer responsibility; an aborted transaction does not publish its feed event.

issues.title: Rejected row branch advances past an unread table
evidence: backend/services/sync_worker.py:3613 advances after rejected rows only when no table was unread; :3622 holds the cursor whenever failed_tables is nonempty.

The preserved independent remediation proof exercised the actual worker cursor branch across nine rejected-row/unread-table combinations. Protocol 2 also emits a single transactional feed rather than independently skipping unread source tables.
remaining: The worker decision proof extracts the actual branch; it is not an installed-device/end-to-end network-outage exercise.

issues.title: Staff/profile push has no durable retry
evidence: backend/services/control_outbox.py:43 flushes intent without committing its caller; staff/profile commands enqueue before their own commit. :77 uses FIFO, backoff and a conditional lease; :169 atomically validates identity, contiguous origin revision and duplicate receipts with the receiver mutation.

backend/services/control_outbox.py:150 purges outbox/origin/receipt/stream state. backend/services/admin_service.py:959 invokes it during purge; backend/routes/auth.py:173 retires/purges the old BizID before rekeying and :176 creates a fresh owner when shared history retains the old identity.

backend/services/sync_worker.py:913 retries control backlog before ordinary idle-skip; :2748 holds synchronization without a cloud-issued credential. backend/routes/sync.py:1138 exposes non-payload pending/error status.

backend/tests/test_sync_protocol_v2.py:85, :95, :116 and :132 verify caller rollback, atomic/idempotent contiguous acknowledgment with valid deletion, FIFO backoff and old-identity quarantine. Included in the 11-pass PostgreSQL run.
remaining: Migrate both receiver and device schemas before resuming control replication; unverifiable pre-protocol intents are cancelled rather than sent under a new identity.

No installed-device process-kill/restart/offline-reconnect drill was performed. Local database encryption/key recovery and production transport/storage controls are separate deployment gates owned by the operations workstream.
